Saints Row started out as pretty much what we can call of "GTA Clone". If before we had a bunch of crazed fools trying to destroy a city, why not an entire game made just for that? Even though the game is made up of stupidty and ridiculousness, Saints Row is actually a good game.
I haven't played the previous releases, and as I don't really follow nor base my opinion on Gameplay videos and other people's reviews, I won't comment on what I do not know.
Either way, Deep Silver is known for releasing games filled with bugs and are only sorted months after released; And yes, the game sometimes bugs out and one does not know what is going on. - I went through it myself, even playing only several months after it's launch. However they weren't game-breaking bugs and never had to restart a mission, nor spend any time shouting and screaming annoyed at the game.

● Graphical wise, they are not really up-to-date nor can they really be compared to some of the previous generation's titles; but I actually like the game's graphical style! Granted I'm not usually one to care and totally base my opinion on a game's graphics. Graphics do NOT make a game good, okey? Okey!
● I enjoyed the Story, even thought I didn't understand it fully (and I still think Deep Silver could actually ship games with Portuguese Language possibility..). I really liked the humour part, really different from what I'm used to with games like GTA, which ended up becoming something quite serious, aiming for extreme reality.
●Regarding the Characters, I found them to be quite charismatic. I found them to be actual supports to a good narrative and not simply prop-adresses there just to be used - like in many other games.
  There were times in which I wish I had played Saints Row: The Third (and I confess it's on my "To-Play List"..). I found the ending to be quite interesting and I am most certainly hoping for yet another Sequel to the story.
 [SPOILER ALERT!!!! - SERIOUSLY!] I really LOVED that I ended up with the bad guy's head on my bare hands!
● The gameplay style of the game is also quite nice - plenty of features that are not really common on other games I've played - especially in certain Main Missions, such as Rescue, Text-Adventure, 2D Platforming and even Stealth! 
  Seriously.. there were times in which I thought to myself "Oh no they didn't!"; Because there are so many surreal things happening that we have to think to ourselves what goes in the mind of someone that thinks about this sort of things. 
  Being fully CO-OP capable is also one of the outstanding features I'd like to talk about. It's certainly way more amusing to play with a friend than alone 
● Not to mention the Soundtrack - it gets to a point of having someone singing "Baby don't hurt me!", out loud at your ears and .. yeah - that's Saints Row for you! One gets to see the real side of the people you play with!
● And yes, before anyone steps forward and shouts that the game is "Too easy" and "Handhelds you" by giving you tons of power and bonuses in the first 20 minutes of the game - and the fact that you can pretty much wreck most enemies during the entire game's duration - some levels are actually tough to get through, especially if one isn't the best player around, or doesn't have help of a friend.

Honestly, I had to honor this game and distinguish it from all the other games I've played in the past. And even though I know plenty of people will disagree with me with the following Score I'll award it with - I'll only give you one advice: Play with a friend. Hopefully a goofy one! Then return to me and tell me what you thought about it now. - I have never laughed so hard at a game before, and I'll even go further and claim I prefer this "GTA Clone" to the actual GTA - but hey, I'll be the first one to admit they are two different games now.

[h1]Series Comparison[/h1]
[b]Saints Row (1)[/b]: Basically a GTA clone. Serious, realistic, dark, gang war here and there, betrayal, and stuff. You know it. And has great story, emotional and deep feel for the game. The Playa rarely speak on this game, which is kinda weird.

[b]Saints Row 2[/b]: Basically Saints Row 1 version 2, it's less serious, a little bit less realistic, more comedic, and more cartoonish if compared to first one, still set in Stillwater, but with different gang. Many mission and activities are basically a joke. Now the Playa officially called The Boss entire time. This game still have a load amount of gang war, up to war with government at the end of game. Still this game has a great deep story and emotional feel. The character customization and clothing is the best of the series.

[b]Saints Row: The Third[/b]: Leaving many basic concept and make a big difference so this is not a GTA clone anymore. Now The Saints is a celebrities, but still criminals inside. The setting now move from Stillwater to Steelport. This game has more sci-fi element (less realistic), less dark but still have a good long story, up to this point this game still have a decent gang war, but the main story is focusing on conflict between The Saints and The Syndicate & STAG. This game has decision making element in some mission, so your choices can affect your future progress. And respect is now like an xp for leveling up. Stupid weapon is what interest me more in Saints Row series, and this game has a lot of it, and now it's official, not from mods. 

[b]Saints Row IV[/b]: I think this game is basically Saints Row 3 version 2. This game take steps further away from it's first game, from the gang war centered story to super hero story. After become a national hero at the ending of previous game, now The Boss is the President of US, but not long after that Earth is invaded by evil alien Zinyak. Many element of the game is now joke from various movies, public stories, other games, and even their previous game. The main concept from this game is so much like The Matrix. And now, because your main mission is inside a simulation, the devs took advantage of it by creating even more outlandish, non-realistic, super & magical power, but funny game. You can even kill peoples with music. And unlike any previous game, there is no gang war, only focus on defeating aliens. Some will say this is just a super hero game with Saints Row character in it.
Epic idiocy strikes again. Good game IMO, but I have no idea why you want to spam me with online connections on a single player game.

[h1]200 character summary[/h1]
Saints Row 4 is an amazing 3rd person free roam action game where you play as the president of the United States, The game is extremely over the top, and somehow the story even manages to top that.

[h1]Story & Characters [b]9/10[/b][/h1]
Like every Saints Row game, The story is completely over the top. The game starts with killing a few terrorists then climbing on a launched nuclear missile, disabling it and then landing right in the presidents chair in the white house. Then the planet gets attacked by aliens you get captured and end up in a simulation. This is where you will spend most of the game, Instead of gangs or STAG you primarily attack aliens in this one. You also visit other simulations, things get pretty crazy.

The characters in the game are all a bit filthy mouthed, But they do all have their own personality, And they are all just as crazy as the story itself, You are forced to play a lot of missions with them, I think the characters are done very well and is obvious by the whole fanbase behind it, Who doesn't like the good kind of crazy?

[h1]Gamemodes & Gameplay [b]9/10[/b][/h1]
The game is single player player or online coop, You can mix and match and play everything in coop, There are a few activities that require a second player, Like Cat and Mouse. The game progresses trough missions which are mostly in the open world, but a lot of the missions are in a special environment, So there is a decent amount of indoor action in the story missions. There are also a bunch of side missions, and some of them are great, but most of them are just clearing up all the activities on the map.

These activities differ in the amount of fun they are, Many of them will be familiar from previous games in the series like Mayhem, These can be on foot or in a vehicle like a tank or a jet, There is a timer and a gold score to achieve, The game stops when you reach the gold score, Which is a shame, this could have been a great opportunity for leaderboards. It does let your combo go on if you do not have the gold score when the timer reaches zero. 

Most of the game is extremely easy, The gold stars are very easy to achieve and missions are just as easy, The game does offer a bunch of challenges but these are mostly getting all gold stars and grinding kills against aliens with a specific weapon. If you like somewhat of a challenge I recommend playing the game on hardcore

Aliens are sadly hard to find in the game, outside of missions and especially endgame there are just none, They will spawn when you cause havoc but also sparsely, especially normal ground troops, You are lucky if you can find more than 2 at a time. It will go from cops to ground troops to jumpers to ufos and tanks and in the final level everything around you will die, including the enemies and a warden spawns, These wardens have a shield which require you to use a superpower to disable it, and then you can damage it, They are pretty easy to kill, But I do think it is a sad thing no other enemies spawn, And it is especially a bummer that your whole wanted level clears when you kill it. Some people just want to kill endlessly, and this is not really the case here.

You have a bunch of superpowers, some enable you to shoot elemental bullets, fire a blast use a powered stomp or pick up thing people and even vehicles with your mind. All these superpowers have different elements, Like Freeze, Fire, Lighting, Even crazier ones like Bling which turns people into gold, Mind control which turns the enemy to your side and gravity, which makes people float. The only thing missing is the ability to fly.

Everything you do earns you exp, With this exp you level up your character which unlocks more and more upgrades, You can upgrade your sprint, jump, but even your homies unlock abilities, upgrade your superpowers, walk on water, no ragdoll and even unlock things like bonus exp and cash, If you upgrade everything you are practically immortal not entirely tho, but there is easy mode and even cheats if you enjoy that kind of thing. For all upgrades including weapons or cars you need cache which is the currency in the game. you need clusters for upgrading your superpowers.

Clusters are one of the collectables in the game, there are 1155 of them and you can collect them all for just an achievement the other collectables do give ingame rewards, The game has 36 statues to destroy and 39 audio logs to collect there are also 8 text adventures, And the DLC brings 2 extra collectable groups in a different simulation.

Like the previous Saints Row games you can customize your character, play as a male or female, adjust skin tone body type, face structure all with nice sliders, You can also still upgrade your weapons, all the classic Saints Row weapons are there, I just prefer normal bullets, But it is nice to be able to go crazy with a dubstep gun if you want to.

[h1]Graphics & Soundtrack [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
The graphics look a bit dated, but it surely is nothing to complain about, What bothers me more is the simulation effect, where cars, buildings everything looks a bit trippy, Like it is glitching. But I guess it fits the game, I just wish it could be turned off. The game has a great soundtrack full with hit singles, and this is mostly what you hear, Even on foot you have some radio built in your head or something. The game has a bit of an original soundtrack, but it is more to enhance certain missions and not something you really listen to while playing the game.

[h1]Performance & Support [b]7/10[/b][/h1]
The ingame graphic settings do not really make a difference for the performance, It is not wonderful but the game runs fine otherwise, For me it hovered between 80 and 120 fps mostly, It depends a lot on the area, The game does run smooth, no stutters or anything like that, so it does not impact gameplay in any way. My Xbox One controller also needed an easy fix, it was mapped wrong, You just need to replace the SDL file in the game directory.

[h1]Endgame & Replayability [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
Endgame you can just cruise around kill some aliens or repeat any of the activities, Sadly you can not replay the missions after you have done them. The activities are pretty easy and highscores are not really a thing, So if you like mindlessly killing or driving around it is okay, But I prefer a goal, or at least something interesting to do and sadly endgame lacks any goal whatsoever.

[h1]Conclusion [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
Overal it is a great game, It is a lot of fun, has a ton of suprises and over the top gameplay. The fun factor does drop a lot after completing the missions but it does offer like 30 hours of gameplay before you reach that point. If Open world cities or crazy stories and gameplay are your thing it is a no brainer, And for the rest, I would recommend to try it, It surely is a lot of fun.

I understand why a lot of people do not like the 4th episode of Volition's critically acclaimed series. With the superpowers we now have the game is a bit too over-the-top. Also, there's no real new area here as the city of Steelport remained the same. It looks a bit different due to the alien invasion (actually, the huge alien ship in the air looks stunning and is pretty cool), but the areas remained the same.

So, in essence, Volition only added a new storyline which now sees our favourite gang pitted against the invading forces of an alien race. And the battle mainly takes place in a Steelport which is not a real city but the virtual reality version of an already destroyed place. So, as a nod to Matrix we, just like Neo, can easily do in this world whatever we want. With the superhuman abilities we can run up on the sides of buildings, can leap forward to great distances and following a charged-up jump we can glide in the air for a long time. This gameplay is similar to the one we had in Prototype so those of you who liked that franchise will see that this one plays pretty familiar.

The downside this approach brings with itself is the fact that as you unlock fast running pretty early own there's no real point in driving any car in the game as getting from point A to point B is much easier by running, jumping and gliding instead of using any vehicles. In fact, later on running right next to people or cars make these fly away due to the sheer force of your fast speed so to a certain degree getting into a car while running is a bit difficult.

However, if you think about it Volition could not have gone in any other direction. After all, in The Third we already kicked the arses of the rival gangs of Steelport and even fought the government's so-called STAG programme. So, taking one step forward was obvious towards aliens. And the jokes and hilarious moments including some excellent cameos of famous people (Keith David, Roddy Piper, Neil Patrick Harris) are still there. 

And this was always the real deal for me: how funny this franchise was, how silly the missions were and how great dialogues the Saints had. When completing the story and the game's many side missions I clocked around the same number of hours I did with The Third. For me, the 4th installment of the Saints did deliver and I think Volition did a great job once again.

It honestly feels like the Saints Row developers heard people say, "Oh, Saints Row? That cartoony, slightly goofier GTA? Yeah, it's cool I guess.", and just take full offense to it. "A little goofy? BULLSHIT. Turn it up to 11, our whole world is a simulation, there are glitches all around, but actually they're features, aliens are invading the real world AND the simulation, also you have super powers and can fly, but here, you can still steal a billion cars and make a sweet ass garage! GTA is a baby game for baby gamers." I wasn't at the table when Saints Row IV was pitched, but I imagine I wasn't far off.

I had my fun in Saints Row 3, but it did always feel like a skewed version of Grand Theft Auto in the sense that it was an open-world game where there were similar criminal-like stories, a random assortment of weapons, (with some added for absurdity, i.e. dildo bat), and the ability to hijack vehicles and commandeer them, assembling your own fleet of whips to cart you around town from mission to mission. However, Saints Row IV totally blew me out of the water with how they revamped nearly everything.

First off, while there is the same "weapon wheel" type gun system, the guns and upgrades in this game are way more out-there than the more grounded arsenal of 3. Due to the game's environment and enemies that you face, I think it really just opened the door for a ton of different options to spice up the game's variety instead of machine gun, machine gun, pistol, bazooka, machine gun. I particularly enjoyed the dubstep gun, which just fired sonic beams and played dubstep as you vaporized nerdz.

Secondly, I loved that the game took place in a simulation, because it was the perfect excuse to just throw superpowers onto your character. I'm not a car guy, so I'd usually just pick up some random car that seemed to go fast, but never really cared enough to customize it or hunt down better vehicles. I loved the power system in this because it immediately gives you super speed and super jumps, which are both able to be upgraded to the point that they can easily compete with any car in the game as far as traversal, and I spent the majority of my playthrough just sprinting from objective to objective.

Honestly it seems like the dev team was just completely unleashed in this entry, and even though all of these new mechanics and ideas were introduced simultaneously, the game is still cohesive and everything flows together. It doesn't feel like you're transitioning from shooter to driver to action RPG, which is great because I think that would've been a very easy pit to fall into with a game that tries to use all of these gameplay elements in tandem.

Also, they still have the dildo bat in this one, and it one-shots. 10/10.

TLDR: Not nearly as good as Saints Row the Third, but still an awesome game.

I personally didn't like the superpower-focused gameplay. I tried to use regular weapons as much as possible, but sometimes using them is mandatory. Also, I REALLY missed driving vehichles - running is way faster than any vehicle now, so there is no point in doing it :/

The story isn't bad, but that whole alien simulation just didn't work for me. Still, it got that amazing Saints Row's  writing and voice acting (provided by an impressive cast, look it up).

Other than being superpower-focused and the whole simulation thing, the game is awesome. The villian is hilarious, you get a lot of good jokes [I literally laughed out loud at least 10 times] and it's a decent platform/shooter game. Definitly worth the asking price.

Fantastic game, full of over the top parodies of many different IPs and dripping with satire. Fun core gameplay, the missions get a bit repetitive - but it's not terribly noticeable while you're exploring.

In short, it utimately depends on whether or not you liked Saints Row The Third or not, but if you did, you will most likely enjoy IV. If not, you're gonna hate this even more than Third.

It's just as whacky, if not, more than Third. None of the Saints Row games ever struck me as hilarious, but I appreciate that the series doesn't take itself very seriously. I'm not joking when I say this game is more fun than Grand Theft Auto V. GTA V may overall be a better game, but it's nowhere near as fun as Saints Row IV. 

Story

The story gets the job done. You're in a simulation, yes it takes place in Steelport still, and you interact with the same characters throught out the Saints series. You have to save all your friends like Pierce, Shaundi, Matt Miller, etc, and defeat Zinyak, the alien ruler who destroyed earth and controls the simulation. There's a lot of nods to Saints Row and Saints Row 2, and there's a lot of familiar flashbacks to the Third game too. You also meet several new characters along the way, though not many.

Second weakest story out of the five games. Gat out of hell takes the cake for being the worst.

Gameplay

I think the gameplay is where SR IV shines. You get super powers in this game like super jumping, flash-like running speed, shoot fire/ice, etc. The jumping and running makes all vehicles completely useless, but I still prefer it and it even makes it hard for me to go back to Saints Row The Third. 

It makes the game real fun though. The gunplay has always been weak in Saints Row, so adding other forms of combat is better. You can also upgrade these powers by collecting data clusters. The data clusters are littered throughout Steelport, and for most of the game, you will not go without seeing at least one on top of some building for the longest. Collect a certain amount and you can spend them on upgrades. I believe there's 1500 total.

You can also upgrade other things just like in Saints Row The Third. Hell, the entire game is honestly just a reskinned SR3, which is fine. Everything you could possibly think of in SR3 is in SRIV.

Missions are nothing to write home about. They're all pretty similar. Save a character, do side missions for characters, rinse and repeat. The side missions are structured in a way to get you to complete the random activities throughout Steelport like taking out flashpoints or hacking all the stores. I will give it to them for making the side missions like that. In any other open world game, I probably wouldn't have done half the stuff I did in this game. More games should do this.

Overall, gameplay is really fun, and I can see myself 100%ing it, or coming close before I get bored.

Overall, it's extremely similar to SR3 with a superhero-like spin to it. Story is nothing special, gameplay is really fun, and graphics are okay I guess.

7/10. Worth it if you like Saints Row and games like Prototype, Infamous, and superhero games.

I enjoy this game a lot. It's essentially just an expansion to Saints Row the Third that goes nuts and gives up any semblance of giving a shit about keeping it grounded. I mean the game gives you superpowers and encourages you to go nuts with them. This game may go off the deep end and is so far removed from the tone of the original two Saints Row games that's its laughable but dammit its fun.

However... I can't recommend it. This port is just broken. It doesn't work cleanly out of the proverbial box and you have to do so much to fix it and even then it still crashes. If you want it, don't buy it from Steam, buy it from GOG. Some of the issues I've had with this port are fixed by disabling steam's in-game overlay and playing in offline mode. Issues the GOG port obviously doesn't have.

Additionally, the game doesn't like Intel CPUs and Nvidia graphics cards so bear in mind that you'll probably have to crack open the Nvidia control panel to fix it (Enable v-sync in game and set V-Sync to Fast in the Nvidia control panel). You might also want to play it in compatibility mode for either windows xp, 7, or 8.
